    • Aligned StarRocks and MySQL session-manager patch signatures
    • Simplified email binary reads, hoisted ModelPrivateAttr, and logged exceptions with explicit exc_info

docs.title: Tests - Atomic Transactions
docs.text:
• StarRocks Atomic BDD Coverage - Expanded sync and async atomic scenarios for StarRocks where shared-nothing SQL transactions are supported.
    • Added StarRocks to update, different entity types, and error-handling outlines (sync and async)
    • Documented shared-nothing limits: nested blocks, multi same-table insert, insert-after-update
    • Capture ORM attrs before insert so expired lazy-loads do not trigger StarRocks error 5307
    • Schema helpers temporarily no-op do_begin during DDL under autocommit

docs.title: Adapters - Redis
docs.text:
• Native FakeAsyncRedis Mock - AsyncRedisMock now uses fakeredis FakeAsyncRedis instead of wrapping sync FakeRedis with AsyncMock.
    • Async commands, pub/sub, and pipelines work through the real async client API
    • CLUSTER mode uses FakeAsyncRedisClusterWrapper with the same cluster helpers as the sync mock
    • Sync and async mocks share a FakeServer across write, read, and search clients
    • Both mocks respect DECODE_RESPONSES from config

docs.title: Tests - Integration
docs.text:
• Flaky Scenario Stabilization - Aligned assertions with implementation and waited for eventual visibility in integration steps.
    • Atomic updates sleep 1s before writing updated_at so database timestamps differ
    • Error-handling steps patch logger.error instead of logger.exception
    • Redis KNN and hybrid search poll until RediSearch indexes a recent write

docs.title: Tests - Redis
docs.text:
• Async Mock Pub/Sub and Pipeline - Added mock rows to async subscribe and pipeline scenario outlines.
    • Async pub/sub channels are unique per adapter_type so mock and container runs do not collide

docs.title: Chore - Agent Rules
docs.text:
• Cursor Agent Guidance - Strengthened workspace rules so agents follow one owner per topic instead of conflicting summaries.
    • Added rules-index.mdc plus canonical models-errors.mdc, helpers-configs.mdc, security.mdc, and contributing.mdc
    • Resolved adapter, lazy-import, and boundary-exception policy into adapter-conventions.mdc
    • Expanded BDD seam/red-green guidance in testing-bdd.mdc; slimmed AGENTS.md to commands and a rule index
    • Changelog writes are opt-in: skip Cursor rules, AGENTS.md, chores, tests-only, and non-consumer docs unless the user asks

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Lockfile - Regenerated uv.lock to the latest compatible versions.
    • boto3 / botocore / boto3-stubs: 1.43.83 → 1.43.89
    • cachetools: 7.1.7 → 7.1.8
    • protobuf: 7.36.0 → 7.36.1
    • psycopg: 3.3.4 → 3.3.5
    • alembic: 1.19.1 → 1.19.2
    • anyio: 4.14.2 → 4.15.0
    • lxml: 6.1.2 → 6.1.3
  • Dev / docs - Updated development and typing stubs.
    • ruff: 0.16.5 → 0.16.6
    • ty: 0.0.76 → 0.0.78
    • types-regex: 2026.8.31.20260831 → 2026.9.3.20260903
    • mkdocstrings-python: 2.0.7 → 2.0.8

docs.title: Helpers - Decorators
docs.text:
• Suffix-less decorator names - retry, timeout, timing, singleton, ttl_cache, grpc_rate_limit and sqlalchemy_atomic, plus postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic, mysql_sqlalchemy_atomic, sqlite_sqlalchemy_atomic and starrocks_sqlalchemy_atomic, are now exported from archipy.helpers.decorators.
    • The old *_decorator names, the async_* names and the old module paths keep working and emit a DeprecationWarning that names the replacement
    • Implementations moved to modules that do not clash with the new function names (for example retry_policy.py and sqlalchemy_transaction.py); see Deprecated names
  • Automatic async detection - retry, timeout, timing, ttl_cache, measure_duration, count_calls, trace_span, trace_root and the SQLAlchemy atomic decorators accept async def functions, so the separate async_* variants are no longer needed.
  • Retry backoff and jitter - retry takes backoff and jitter, and validates max_retries, delay, backoff and jitter when the decorator is applied.

docs.title: Configs - Email
docs.text: • EMAIL.CONNECTION_REFRESH_SECONDS - Replaces the hard-coded TOKEN_REFRESH_SECONDS constant; controls how long an SMTP connection is reused before it is reconnected.

docs.title: Configs - Keycloak
docs.text: • KEYCLOAK.TOKEN_LEEWAY_SECONDS - Leeway in seconds applied when decoding tokens locally (default 0).

docs.title: Adapters - Email
docs.text:
• BREAKING: send failures raise UnavailableError - After the retries are used up, a failed send now raises UnavailableError instead of being swallowed.
    • The broken SMTP session is closed before each retry, and the message is sent in the same attempt after reconnecting
    • Oversized attachments map to InvalidArgumentError
    • STARTTLS is negotiated only when the server advertises it, so plain SMTP relays work

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text:
• BREAKING: expired tokens raise TokenExpiredError - Local decoding no longer applies python-keycloak's implicit 60 second leeway, so a recently expired token fails with TokenExpiredError instead of surfacing as INVALID_CREDENTIALS from UserInfo.
    • Set KEYCLOAK.TOKEN_LEEWAY_SECONDS to restore a grace period
    • Role checks read UserInfo, which needs the "Add to userinfo" mapper option in Keycloak

docs.title: Adapters - Saman IPG
docs.text: • BREAKING: HTTP 5xx maps to UnavailableError - Server errors from the gateway are no longer reported as generic failures. TERMINAL_ID is validated as numeric.

docs.title: Helpers - Decorators
docs.text:
• timeout for async and threads - Async functions are bounded with asyncio.timeout. A synchronous function called outside the main thread raises FailedPreconditionError instead of running without a limit. Float seconds are supported and the previous SIGALRM handler and timer are restored.
  • retry semantics - max_retries is documented as the total number of attempts, and max_retries=0 now raises InvalidArgumentError when the decorator is applied instead of never calling the function.
  • singleton returns the class - isinstance checks and subclassing keep working on the decorated name.
  • ttl_cache thread safety - Cache access is guarded by a lock, keys include argument types, calls with unhashable arguments bypass the cache, and same-named cached methods in a class hierarchy no longer collide.
  • timing logging - Logs at DEBUG or lower, also when the function raises.

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text: • Cheaper metric decorators - measure_duration and count_calls read the config once per call and resolve instrument names when the decorator is applied.

docs.title: Helpers - Decorators
docs.text:
• Atomic blocks and cancellation - CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit pass through sqlalchemy_atomic unchanged instead of becoming InternalError, and a failing rollback no longer hides the original error.
    • The atomic marker is cleared when the outermost block exits
    • MySQL error codes map to deadlock, timeout and constraint errors
    • @sqlalchemy_atomic_decorator(db_type=...) with parentheses no longer fails with got multiple values for argument 'db_type'
  • Telemetry failures - An exporter error while recording a metric no longer replaces the function result, and interrupts are recorded with status cancelled.
  • trace_span and trace_class - Nested classes are left untouched, and capture_args lets the function raise its own error when the call arguments cannot be bound.
  • Retry exhaustion - The last exception is chained as the cause of ResourceExhaustedError.

docs.title: Helpers - gRPC
docs.text: • rpc.server.active_requests on cancelled streams - The recorder's finish is idempotent and runs when a sync streaming RPC terminates, so cancelled or never-iterated streams no longer leave the counter incremented.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text: • Expired token handling - See the TokenExpiredError change above.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• BDD coverage - Added scenarios for the email, Parsian IPG and Saman IPG adapters, the decorators, the Singleton metaclass, Keycloak auth dependencies and the gRPC helpers.
  • Real containers - The email feature runs against Mailpit containers (STARTTLS and plain SMTP), and the KeycloakUtils and AuthContextManager scenarios use real Keycloak tokens.
  • Merged features - Retry, timeout, timing and deprecation scenarios live in decorators.feature, and the gRPC rate-limit identifier and client interceptor scenarios in grpc_helpers.feature.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text: • Reviewer nits - Fixed a pyproject.toml comment typo, added reasons to ty ignores and broad except blocks, used DatetimeUtils in the email adapter, and gave the TOTP secret-generation error an operation detail.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • Raised lower bounds - pydantic>=2.14.1 and jdatetime>=6.1.1, matching uv.lock.

docs.title: Configs - Auth
docs.text: • AUTH.JWT_LEEWAY - Clock-skew tolerance in seconds applied to exp, nbf and iat when verifying tokens (default 0).

docs.title: Configs - Keycloak
docs.text: • KEYCLOAK.REMOTE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS - Opt-in cache for UserInfo and UMA permission lookups in KeycloakUtils (default 0, off). A revoked token stays accepted for up to this long when enabled.

docs.title: Helpers - Utils
docs.text:
• verify_totp replay guard - verify_totp takes an optional replay_guard(step) callable that is called with the matched time step for a valid code. Returning False rejects the code.
  • keep_zwnj option - clean_spacing and normalize_persian_text can keep the zero-width non-joiner instead of turning it into a space.

docs.title: Helpers - Interceptors
docs.text:
• request_validation() - Context manager exported from archipy.helpers.interceptors.grpc.exception; a Pydantic ValidationError raised inside it is reported as INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  • trusted_proxy_hosts - The rate-limit interceptors read x-forwarded-for only when the direct peer is a trusted proxy, so callers behind a load balancer no longer share one bucket.

docs.title: Helpers - Utils
docs.text:
• BREAKING: HMAC signing keys have a minimum length - JWTUtils raises InvalidArgumentError when SECRET_KEY is shorter than RFC 7518 requires: 32 bytes for HS256, 48 for HS384 and 64 for HS512. It checks on both create and decode, and refuses the none algorithm.
  • Password hash format - Hashes are stored as pbkdf2_sha256$iterations$salt$hash, and the default AUTH.HASH_ITERATIONS is now 600000.
    • Hashes in the old format still verify, using the configured iterations and then 100000
    • PASSWORD_HISTORY_SIZE=0 disables the history check, and negative values are rejected
  • TOTP expiry and secrets - generate_totp reports an expiry no later than the end of the verification window. Secrets that are valid base32 are decoded, so authenticator apps produce matching codes.
  • BREAKING: additional_claims cannot redefine registered claims - JWTUtils.create_token and the token helpers raise InvalidArgumentError when additional_claims contains iss, aud, jti or any key already set by the token data (for example sub, type and token_version). Time claims such as exp can still be overridden.
  • Persian punctuation - normalize_punctuation converts ASCII ,, ?, ;, % and _ only next to Persian text, so numbers (1,000), URLs, e-mails and identifiers are left intact. remove_punctuation still strips them.

docs.title: Helpers - Interceptors
docs.text:
• BREAKING: handler ValidationError maps to INTERNAL - A Pydantic ValidationError raised by handler code is a server fault, so it is no longer reported as INVALID_ARGUMENT.
    • Wrap request parsing in request_validation() to keep INVALID_ARGUMENT
    • Pass validation_errors_as_invalid_argument=True to the exception interceptors to restore the old mapping
  • Interceptor order - customized_interceptors accepts a sequence and keeps its order; a set still works but has no guaranteed order.
  • Rate-limit startup - A failed rate-limit setup raises when GRPC_RATE_LIMIT.FAIL_CLOSED is set instead of starting an unprotected server.

docs.title: Helpers - Interceptors
docs.text:
• Deliberate aborts are kept - The sync exception interceptor no longer rewrites context.abort() (for example RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED from the rate limiter) to INTERNAL, and the async one no longer aborts a second time after AbortError.
  • Internal details stay server-side - Unexpected errors send a bare InternalError; the error text, type and method names are no longer put in trailing metadata. Validation errors no longer echo the submitted input, and trailing metadata is capped at 4096 bytes and serialized with default=str.
  • Rate limits behind other interceptors - The base interceptor closures use functools.wraps, so decorated RPCs are still limited when a custom interceptor follows the rate limiter.
  • Rate-limit edge cases - A handler that returns None no longer runs twice when failing open, a rejected call refunds the quota of earlier windows, a failing identifier_fn skips limiting instead of pooling callers, and JWT verification runs off the event loop. Window metadata and the auth config are cached.
  • Metrics statuses - Cancelled RPCs and closed streams are recorded as cancelled, the final gRPC status code is recorded as rpc.grpc.status_code, and handled client errors count as ok.
  • generic_exception_handler - Records the real exception instead of a bare UnknownError.
  • Rate-limit windows - Negative time components are rejected.

docs.title: Helpers - Utils
docs.text:
• TOTP - The code length comes from TOTP_LENGTH, so a one-digit code can no longer match, and non-ASCII digits are rejected instead of raising TypeError.
  • Keycloak auth - grpc_auth and async_grpc_auth support streaming handlers and keep the auth context through the stream, aborts pass through, token parsing is case-insensitive on the scheme and rejects repeated or empty authorization values, and failure causes are logged instead of sent to the client.
  • OTel - A failed initialization retries only after a 30 second back-off, shut-down providers are tracked in a WeakSet, the Pushgateway loop sends a final push on shutdown, and the shared instrument cache is locked.
  • Datetime - A %z offset parsed from a string is kept, the holiday cache is locked and bounded, daterange counts calendar dates, and a non-JSON holiday response raises UnknownError.
  • Strings - Noon and Zal tables no longer corrupt text, snake_to_camel_case keeps inner capitals, replace_numbers_with_mask works in one pass, the currency mask no longer matches backslashes, and punctuation spacing no longer splits file.txt.
  • Files and national codes - Allowed extensions match case-insensitively and with a leading dot; the national-code validator rejects non-ASCII digits and repeated-digit codes.
  • Singleton - Uses a reentrant lock, so a singleton can build another singleton.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • BDD coverage - Added scenarios to the existing TOTP, password, JWT, datetime, string, file, base utils, singleton, error handling, app utils, gRPC helpers, rate-limit, OTel and Keycloak features, including real in-process sync and async gRPC servers for the abort, metrics and rate-limit behavior.

docs.title: Configs - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• OTEL.INSTRUMENTATION_SKIP_DEP_CHECK - Libraries that are instrumented even when the installed version is newer than the range the instrumentor declares (default ["sqlalchemy"]). opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy still declares sqlalchemy<2.1.0, while ArchiPy requires SQLAlchemy 2.1, so SQLAlchemy produced no spans before.
    • ArchiPy logs one warning naming the mismatch when it applies the bypass
    • Set the option to [] to turn the bypass off, and remove a key once its instrumentor supports the version

docs.title: Configs - Temporal
docs.text: • TEMPORAL.METRICS_PULL_PORT - Port of the Temporal SDK /metrics scrape endpoint (default 8201). With OTEL.METRICS_EXPORTER=pull the SDK serves its own endpoint on OTEL.METRICS_PULL_HOST and this port. The port must differ from OTEL.METRICS_PULL_PORT.

docs.title: Adapters - Email
docs.text: • email.send span - EmailAdapter.send_email records a client span with server.address, server.port, network.protocol.name, email.tls_mode, email.recipient_count and email.attachment_count. Credentials, addresses, subject and body never reach a span. No OpenTelemetry instrumentor exists for smtplib.

docs.title: Adapters - MinIO
docs.text:
• Folders in non-recursive list_objects - A non-recursive listing now also returns one entry per "folder" directly below the prefix (object_name ends with /, size is 0). Every entry carries is_prefix.
    • Callers that expect only objects should skip entries where is_prefix is true

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text: • Pushgateway exporter - The Temporal SDK cannot push to a Pushgateway. With OTEL.METRICS_EXPORTER=pushgateway its metrics still go over OTLP to OTEL.OTLP_ENDPOINT, and a warning says so.

docs.title: Helpers - Utils
docs.text: • Instrumentor version conflicts are visible - An instrumentor that refuses an installed library version was logged at debug level, so the service ran without spans and without a message. It is now a warning that names the library and says no spans will be emitted. A library that is not installed at all is still skipped at debug level.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text: • Sync engines are traced - The session manager bound create_engine at import time, before OpenTelemetry replaced it, so sync engines never emitted query spans. It is now looked up when the engine is created.

docs.title: Adapters - Kafka
docs.text: • Producers and consumers are traced - Producer and Consumer were bound at import time and bypassed the OpenTelemetry instrumentor. They are now looked up when the client is created, which also covers the async adapters.

docs.title: Adapters - Redis
docs.text: • Search with OpenTelemetry enabled - opentelemetry-instrumentation-redis reads the FT.SEARCH reply as a list, but RESP3, the default, returns a dict, so it raised KeyError inside the caller's search. The instrumentor helper is now guarded so an unreadable reply never reaches the application.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text: • Denied UMA permissions - When every requested permission is denied, Keycloak answers 403 not_authorized. check_permissions_batch raised InternalError for it, so fastapi_auth answered 500. It now returns an empty set and the request is rejected with PERMISSION_DENIED.

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text: • Tracing interceptor - TracingInterceptor used the first global tracer provider, so spans were lost after OpenTelemetry was re-initialized. It now uses the tracer ArchiPy currently owns.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Real containers for telemetry - New OpenTelemetry Collector and Pushgateway test containers replace in-memory exporters, stub gateways and mocked Temporal clients in otel.feature.
  • Adapter spans - Spans are verified through the collector for Redis (sync and async), Kafka (sync and async), MinIO, ScyllaDB (sync and async), Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and StarRocks (sync and async), Keycloak, Elasticsearch, Vault, Email and Temporal, plus Temporal worker and client metrics.
  • No mocks for Keycloak and gRPC - The Keycloak utils, gRPC rate limit and app_utils scenarios run against the real Keycloak container, real gRPC servers and the Redis container.
  • MinIO - New scenarios cover stat_object, listing by prefix, presigned PUT uploads, error mapping and caches.
  • HTTP clients - Test code uses httpx2 instead of requests and urllib.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text: • Instrumentor compatibility check - make check-instrumentor-compat and a weekly workflow resolve each instrumentor's instruments extra together with ArchiPy's own bound with uv. The workflow fails once upstream supports the required version, the signal to drop the bypass.

docs.title: Adapters - Kafka
docs.text:
• Consume span ends at the commit - The Kafka instrumentor opens a <topic> process span when a message is polled and ended it only on the next poll, consume or close. The span then covered idle time and stayed the current span of the thread, so unrelated spans became its children. KafkaConsumerAdapter.commit now ends it.
    • batch_consume produces one span for the whole batch, with a link to every message; commit once after the batch
    • A consumer that never commits, such as one with ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT=true, keeps the previous behaviour
    • The async consumer adapter is unchanged, because its polls run in an executor thread

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Kafka consume spans - New scenarios cover a batch, one message at a time, consecutive polls without a commit and auto-commit, against the real Kafka container and the OpenTelemetry Collector.
  • Test isolation - The Kafka span scenarios no longer leave an open span that made a later scenario record a span despite a sample ratio of zero. ConfluentKafkaInstrumentor.uninstrument does not unwrap consume or close, so binding it again wrapped consume twice and one batch produced two consume spans, the first never ended. The test cleanup now unwraps them. Production binds the instrumentor once and is not affected.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text:
• Type checker - ty 0.0.87 reports narrowed field overrides in the SQLite and StarRocks configs, so those two fields carry a documented ty: ignore.
  • Kafka tutorial - Describes how consume spans end for batches, single messages and auto-commit.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • Lock file and lower bounds - uv.lock is refreshed and the lower bounds follow it: async-lru>=2.4.0 (Keycloak, MinIO and ScyllaDB packages), boto3>=1.43.113 (MinIO package), and the development tools boto3-stubs>=1.43.113, pre-commit>=4.7.0 and ty>=0.0.87. Transitive updates: botocore 1.43.113, botocore-stubs 1.43.113, markdown 3.11.1, sentry-sdk 2.72.0, starlette 1.8.0, truststore 0.10.5, types-s3transfer 0.19.2 and wrapt 2.5.1.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Count threshold - execute_search_query accepts a keyword-only count_threshold. The total is exact up to that many rows. Above it, PostgreSQL returns the planner estimate (EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)) instead of scanning every row. MySQL, SQLite and StarRocks still count exactly.
    • The estimate never falls below the rows already counted, and a query that cannot be estimated falls back to the exact count
  • Count cache - With COUNT_CACHE_ENABLED=true the total of a search is cached for COUNT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, so only the first page of a search runs a COUNT and later pages reuse the total. The sync adapters use ttl_cache and the async adapters use alru_cache, so it needs the cache extra. The cache is off by default, and a total can be stale for up to the TTL.

docs.title: Configs - SQLAlchemy
docs.text: • Count settings - COUNT_CACHE_ENABLED (default false), COUNT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 60), COUNT_CACHE_MAX_SIZE (default 1000) and COUNT_THRESHOLD (default unset, always exact) are added to SQLAlchemyConfig and to .env.example for the SQLAlchemy, MySQL, SQLite and StarRocks configs.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Cheaper search totals - execute_search_query skips the COUNT when there is no pagination or the first page is not full. Otherwise the COUNT reads only the entity primary key and drops the ORDER BY, so the database can answer from the primary key index. A query with DISTINCT, GROUP BY, HAVING, LIMIT, OFFSET or FETCH keeps its own columns, because they change the row count.
  • Filter expressions - _apply_filter builds its expressions from one module-level map instead of a dict of 15 lambdas on every call. IS_NOT_NULL uses is_not.
  • Shared helpers - The sync and async adapters share the entity type checks and the entity extraction of execute_search_query, and _handle_db_exception lowers the error message once.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • Search totals - New scenarios in atomic_transactions.feature cover totals across pages, which pages run a COUNT, DISTINCT, GROUP BY and LIMIT queries, the exact and estimated totals around the threshold, the cache keys and TTL (sync and async) and every filter operation, with the rejection of a non-list value for list filters. They run on PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and StarRocks.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text: • Search totals tutorial - New SQLAlchemy Search Totals tutorial, linked from the PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and StarRocks tutorials and from the adapters index.

docs.title: Models - DTOs
docs.text:
• Search output DTOs - SearchOutputDTO carries total_count and a computed total_count_estimated. With a count threshold the total is exact up to the threshold and a PostgreSQL estimate above it, and the estimate is always above the threshold, so total_count_estimated is true when total_count is above the COUNT_THRESHOLD of the SQLAlchemy config. An API can show "10000+" instead of an invented number.
    • It reads POSTGRES_SQLALCHEMY by default. A subclass sets count_threshold_config for another config. Without a global config or a threshold the flag is false.
    • ExactSearchOutputDTO has the same fields with total_count_estimated always false, for searches that count on their own.

docs.title: Configs - Pagination
docs.text: • PaginationConfig - New PAGINATION config on BaseConfig with MAX_ITEMS (default 10000), set with PAGINATION__MAX_ITEMS. It is the deepest page * page_size a PaginationDTO accepts.

docs.title: Models - DTOs
docs.text: • PaginationDTO limit from config - PaginationDTO.MAX_ITEMS is None by default and the limit comes from PAGINATION.MAX_ITEMS of the global config, or from the PaginationConfig default when no global config is set. A subclass that sets its own MAX_ITEMS keeps it.

docs.title: Configs - SQLAlchemy
docs.text: • Default COUNT_THRESHOLD - BaseConfig.set_global() fills an unset COUNT_THRESHOLD of the SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and StarRocks configs with PAGINATION.MAX_ITEMS. A search on PostgreSQL now returns an estimated total above 10000 rows instead of counting them, where it used to count exactly. Set COUNT_THRESHOLD to a larger number to count exactly for longer.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • Search output DTO and pagination config - New scenarios in atomic_transactions.feature cover the estimated and exact flags around the threshold on PostgreSQL. New scenarios in base_config.feature cover the default threshold from PAGINATION.MAX_ITEMS, an explicit threshold winning over it and the pagination limit following it.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text: • Docs - The search totals tutorial explains the default threshold and the search output DTOs, and the API reference lists search_output_dto and PaginationConfig.

docs.title: Helpers - Errors
docs.text:
• archipy.helpers.errors package - One home for error handling on both transports.
    • capture_exception, format_validation_errors, request_validation, invalid_argument_from_validation and resolve_error (maps any exception to the BaseError a client should see).
    • archipy.helpers.errors.fastapi: setup_exception_handlers, handle_fastapi_exception, handle_unexpected_exception, create_error_response and get_fastapi_exception_responses.
    • archipy.helpers.errors.grpc: GrpcExceptionInterceptor, abort_grpc and grpc_status_code.
  • GrpcExceptionInterceptor - One name for both kinds of server: GrpcExceptionInterceptor() is the sync interceptor and GrpcExceptionInterceptor(aio=True) the grpc.aio one. The sync and async variants share one error mapping instead of repeating it.
  • abort_grpc(error, context) - Replaces BaseError.abort_grpc_sync and abort_grpc_async. It detects a sync or grpc.aio context; on an async context use await abort_grpc(error, context).
  • validation_errors_as_internal - New keyword on AppUtils.create_grpc_app and create_async_grpc_app.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• gRPC validation errors - A Pydantic ValidationError raised by a gRPC handler is now reported as INVALID_ARGUMENT, the counterpart of the HTTP 422 the FastAPI handlers return. It used to be INTERNAL. Pass validation_errors_as_internal=True to keep the old mapping.
  • FastAPI handler - A BaseError handled through handle_fastapi_exception is now logged and recorded on the current OTel span, like the registered handlers already did.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Error handling moved - The FastAPI handlers left app_utils.py and the gRPC interceptor left helpers/interceptors/grpc/exception/. BaseError no longer imports grpc; http_status and grpc_status stay plain class attributes.
  • Removed (internal only) - FastAPIExceptionHandler, FastAPIUtils.setup_exception_handlers, GrpcServerExceptionInterceptor, AsyncGrpcServerExceptionInterceptor, BaseError.abort_grpc_sync, abort_grpc_async, abort_with_error_sync, abort_with_error_async, ErrorUtils.handle_grpc_exception, BaseUtils.format_validation_errors and archipy.models.dtos.fastapi_exception_response_dto. Apps that use AppUtils.create_fastapi_app, create_grpc_app and create_async_grpc_app are not affected.
  • Shared deprecation helper - deprecated_alias and warn_deprecated_name moved to archipy.helpers._deprecation.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
• BaseUtils.capture_exception - use archipy.helpers.errors.capture_exception.
  • BaseUtils.async_handle_fastapi_exception - use archipy.helpers.errors.fastapi.handle_fastapi_exception.
  • BaseUtils.get_fastapi_exception_responses - use archipy.helpers.errors.fastapi.get_fastapi_exception_responses.

Each emits a DeprecationWarning that names the replacement and returns the same result.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • The gRPC validation scenarios in error_handling.feature now expect INVALID_ARGUMENT by default and INTERNAL with the opt-out. Test steps use the new archipy.helpers.errors paths.

docs.title: Chore
docs.text: • Docs - New errors API reference page; the interceptors, utils, error handling and observability tutorials use the new paths.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Several databases of the same type - Session managers are keyed by configuration, so two adapters built with different configs no longer share the first one's engine.
    • The same config still returns the same manager.
    • sqlalchemy_atomic and the *_sqlalchemy_atomic shortcuts take an optional registry.
    • Every registry subclass has its own manager slots, so a subclass of a concrete registry can hold another database of the same type.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text:
• archipy.adapters.keycloak.auth - fastapi_auth and grpc_auth are plain functions with __all__.
    • fastapi_auth returns an always-async dependency that works for def and async def endpoints; grpc_auth detects async def servicer methods.
    • fastapi_auth also sets AuthContextManager for the request and clears it when the request ends. set_auth_context returns a token and clear_auth_context accepts it, so a nested guard restores the outer caller.
    • AuthenticatedUserDTO gains token_info.

docs.title: Helpers - gRPC
docs.text: • Rate-limit counter store - RateLimitStore and AsyncRateLimitStore protocols and a store argument on the rate-limit interceptors, plus store_errors for failures of a caller's backend. Without them the Redis default is built lazily as before.

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• Configurable SDK - OpentelemetryConfig gains TRACES_SAMPLER, PROPAGATORS (including b3 and b3multi), OTLP_COMPRESSION, SPAN_BATCH_*, LOG_BATCH_*, SERVICE_VERSION, SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID, RESOURCE_DETECTORS and METRICS_DURATION_BUCKETS_S.
    • Service instance id, host and os are detected by default; process is opt-in because it records the command line. Explicit resource settings override detected attributes.
    • With USE_STANDARD_ENV, the standard OTEL_* variables fill in the settings the config leaves unset; an explicitly set field wins, and invalid values are logged and ignored. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true keeps the SDK off.
    • Defaults are queue 4096, batch 512 and compression none. A batch size left unset follows a lowered queue.
  • B3 propagation - opentelemetry-propagator-b3 ships in archipy[otel].
  • OtelRuntime - The provider state lives on runtime instances; OtelUtils is a typed facade over a default one, with runtime() and set_runtime().
  • Decorator attributes - Spans record code.function.name and, for a failed call, error.type; the measure_duration and count_calls instruments add error.type to a call that ends in error or cancelled.

docs.title: Models - DTOs
docs.text: • RpcInstrumentsDTO - Frozen DTO for the gRPC metric instruments.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• gRPC server metrics (breaking) - The histogram is now rpc.server.call.duration (was rpc.server.request.duration) with rpc.system.name, the fully qualified rpc.method, rpc.response.status_code and error.type for server-failure codes. A handler that raises without a status is recorded as UNKNOWN. rpc.server.active_requests stays on the same attributes. Update dashboards and alerts.
  • fastapi_auth is always async - It works for both endpoint kinds, so async_fastapi_auth and async_grpc_auth are deprecated aliases.
  • Type strictness - JWTUtils raises InvalidTokenError for a non-string sub or an invalid exp claim. Helpers, interceptors, errors and decorators replace Any with precise types, ParamSpec and Protocols.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Enforced layer order - models ← configs ← helpers ← adapters is checked by an import-linter contract in make lint and pre-commit. Models read settings through archipy.models.runtime_settings, and the Persian digit table is archipy.models.types.PersianDigitType.
  • Atomic decorators moved - They live in archipy.adapters.base.sqlalchemy.atomic.
  • OTel internals split - OtelUtils internals moved into the private archipy.helpers.utils._otel package.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
All removed in 6.0.0; each warning names the replacement.

  • archipy.helpers.decorators atomic names (sqlalchemy_atomic and the *_sqlalchemy_atomic shortcuts) - use archipy.adapters.base.sqlalchemy.atomic.
  • archipy.helpers.utils.keycloak_utils and KeycloakUtils - use archipy.adapters.keycloak.auth.
  • KeycloakUtils.async_fastapi_auth and async_grpc_auth - use fastapi_auth and grpc_auth.
  • Reading request.state.user_info, token_info, actor_chain and user_roles - read them from AuthContextManager.

docs.title: Models - Errors
docs.text:
• Resource Exhausted Error - Added DatabaseResourceExhaustedError for a database server that runs out of memory or connections.
    • HTTP status 503 and gRPC status RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
  • Unknown Outcome Error - Added DatabaseUnknownOutcomeError for PostgreSQL 40003 (statement_completion_unknown), where the statement may or may not have completed.
  • Retryable Flag - Added the retryable class attribute to DatabaseError, False by default.
    • True on DatabaseSerializationError, DatabaseDeadlockError and DatabaseResourceExhaustedError

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Driver Error Classification - Database errors are now classified by the driver error code before the message text.
    • Added archipy/adapters/base/sqlalchemy/driver_errors.py, used by the adapter mixin and the atomic decorators
    • Reads PostgreSQL SQLSTATE, MySQL and StarRocks errno, and SQLite error names
    • Falls back to DBAPIError.connection_invalidated for a disconnect with no usable code
    • StarRocks memory-limit errors reported under errno 1064 are matched by message, except syntax errors
    • The message fallback is unchanged for drivers that expose no code
  • Driver Error Logging - The driver code, message, detail, constraint and table are logged once where the domain error is raised.
    • Serialization failures, deadlocks and resource exhaustion log at WARNING, everything else at ERROR
    • Fields follow the OpenTelemetry names db.response.status_code, error.type and db.query.text
    • The statement is logged only at DEBUG, with string and numeric literals replaced by ?
    • Bind parameters are never logged, and no driver detail is added to additional_data
  • Atomic Block Errors - Raw SQLAlchemy errors in the atomic block are classified by code, where every OperationalError used to become DatabaseConnectionError.

docs.title: Models - Errors
docs.text:
• Catchable as Query Error - DatabaseConnectionError, DatabaseTimeoutError, DatabaseConstraintError, DatabaseIntegrityError, DatabaseDeadlockError, DatabaseSerializationError, DatabaseResourceExhaustedError and DatabaseUnknownOutcomeError now extend DatabaseQueryError.
    • Existing except DatabaseQueryError blocks keep catching errors that the classification now reports under a specific class
    • A DatabaseQueryError handler placed before a more specific handler now shadows it

docs.title: Helpers - Errors
docs.text: • Captured Exception Log - capture_exception now logs the exception type and message.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:

    • The mapping in atomic.py was never reached for errors raised inside adapter methods
    • HTTP status changes from 500 to 409 and gRPC status from INTERNAL to ABORTED

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• Replay-Safe Providers - When temporalio is installed the OpenTelemetry runtime builds Temporal's replay-safe tracer and meter providers, and falls back to the plain SDK providers otherwise.
    • All Temporal-specific code sits in archipy/helpers/utils/_otel/temporal_providers.py
    • Adoption of an existing global provider recognises the replay-safe wrappers
    • The tracer provider is published globally whenever the tracer global is still unset, even if another signal already set its own
    • behavior: with temporalio installed, OtelUtils.tracer_provider() and OtelUtils.meter_provider() return wrappers that do not expose the SDK sampler, resource or span processor attributes
    • The logger provider stays unwrapped because ReplaySafeLoggerProvider cannot be instantiated with opentelemetry-api 1.45

docs.title: Tests - Adapters
docs.text:
• Temporal Tracing - Added scenarios for the messaging attributes, the client plugin, the sandbox passthrough and the stock plugin side by side.
    • A real Temporal container checks that tracing is disabled, and workflows still run, when a plain tracer provider was registered first
  • OpenTelemetry Providers - Added scenarios for adopting a replay-safe tracer provider, publishing the tracer provider when traces are enabled later, and plain SDK providers when temporalio is not installed.

docs.title: Tests - Adapters
docs.text:
• Elastic APM Server Scenarios - Added scenarios that send telemetry to a real Elastic APM Server and check what Elasticsearch stored.
    • Scenario Outlines with a route column run every case twice: the application exports to APM Server directly, and through a collector that forwards to it
    • Covered adapters: Redis, Kafka, Elasticsearch, MinIO, SQLAlchemy (PostgreSQL, MySQL, StarRocks, SQLite), ScyllaDB, Vault, Keycloak, httpx2 and Temporal
    • Temporal activities are asserted as messaging transactions, Redis and SQLAlchemy calls as db spans, Kafka as messaging
    • Temporal SDK metrics, decorator metrics (count_calls, measure_duration), gRPC and FastAPI server metrics and log records correlated with their trace id are checked in Elasticsearch

docs.title: Chore - Test Infrastructure
docs.text:
• Elastic APM Test Containers - Added an Elastic APM Server test container with its own Elasticsearch, and a collector container that forwards to it.
    • Standalone APM Server runs without Kibana
    • Elasticsearch and APM Server test images are 9.5.5
  • Shared Telemetry Containers - scripts/behave_parallel.py starts the collector and the Elastic APM stack once and shares them with every feature process through ARCHIPY_SHARED_TELEMETRY.
    • Each scenario exports under its own service.name, so scenarios sharing the containers do not see each other
    • Only the parts the selected features ask for through their tags are started
  • Elasticsearch Test Container Restart - The Elasticsearch test container builds a fresh container when it is started again after a stop, so features can run back to back in one process.
  • Image Pre-Pull - Added make pull-test-images, which pulls every image listed in .env.test, four at a time.

docs.title: Configs - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:

  • OtelLogsExporter enum - Unique logs exporter via LOGS_EXPORTER (console | otlp); default console splits INFO/DEBUG → stdout and WARNING+ → stderr
  • LOGS_ENABLED default true - Log export on when OTel is enabled (console by default; switch to otlp for collectors)
  • METRICS_PULL_PORT default 8200 - Default scrape bind port for pull metrics
  • SYSTEM_METRICS_ENABLED - Kill switch for SystemMetricsInstrumentor (default true when metrics are on)

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text:
• Messaging Attributes on Workflow Spans - MessagingOpenTelemetryInterceptor marks the worker-side workflow spans as messaging process operations on the workflow task queue.
    • Covers RunWorkflow, HandleSignal, HandleQuery, ValidateUpdate and HandleUpdate, so Elastic APM shows transaction.type = messaging instead of unknown
    • Overrides temporalio's private _workflow_maybe_span and forwards any arguments to it; workflow_interceptor_class raises ConfigurationError at startup when temporalio no longer provides it
    • Replay is unaffected because the replay-safe tracer produces non-recording spans
  • Messaging Attributes on Start-Side Spans - StartWorkflow, StartActivity, StartChildWorkflow, StartUpdateWithStartWorkflow and the client-side StartActivity spans carry messaging send attributes with the target task queue as destination.
    • Activities and child workflows started without a task queue use the workflow's own queue
  • Messaging Attributes on Client Signal, Query and Update Spans - SignalWorkflow, QueryWorkflow and StartWorkflowUpdate carry send attributes without a destination.
    • The destination is left out on purpose: Elastic APM turns messaging.destination.name into a service-map node and workflow ids are unbounded

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text:
• Attributes Skipped Without Temporal Spans - With add_temporal_spans=False no messaging attributes are set, so the caller's span (for example an HTTP request) is never marked.
  • Behavior - Temporal workflow, signal, query and update transactions report transaction.type = messaging in Elastic APM instead of unknown, and the start-side client spans report messaging span types.

docs.title: Tests - Adapters
docs.text:
• Order Saga Scenarios - Added OrderSagaWorkflow and NotificationWorkflow with reserve, charge, ship and notify activities and their compensations.
    • Payment succeeds on a chosen attempt, so retries produce one RunActivity per attempt
    • Shipping failure or the cancel signal reverts the completed steps in reverse order
    • The approve and cancel signals, the get_state query, the add_note update with a validator, a child workflow, update-with-start and a standalone activity are covered
  • Trace and Elastic APM Assertions - Collector scenarios check span names, one shared trace id and the messaging attributes; Elastic APM scenarios check transaction and span types, parent links and three RunActivity:charge_payment transactions for three attempts.
    • Added steps for a named APM span and for a count of named transactions

docs.title: Models - Keycloak DTOs
docs.text:
• Keycloak DTO Package - Added archipy.models.dtos.keycloak with pydantic DTOs for every Keycloak admin REST representation the adapter uses, generated from the Keycloak admin OpenAPI spec.
    • KeycloakBaseDTO is standalone and does not derive from BaseDTO, whose extra="ignore" would hide typos and drop fields newer Keycloak versions add
    • Request DTOs (Keycloak*RequestDTO) forbid unknown fields, matching the Unrecognized field 400 that Keycloak answers
    • Response DTOs (Keycloak*DTO) keep unknown fields in model_extra
    • Dict-style access on responses (result["id"], result.get("id")) and dict payloads still work and emit a DeprecationWarning until 6.0.0
  • Typed Results - Create, update, delete and assign calls return KeycloakCreateResultDTO, KeycloakUpdateResultDTO, KeycloakDeleteResultDTO or KeycloakAssignResultDTO instead of a dict or bytes.
    • Create results carry the id of the new resource, found by lookup because Keycloak answers with an empty body
    • skip_exists creates report msg == "Already exists" and no id
  • Typed Token Data - Tokens, UserInfo, decoded and introspected claims, the discovery document and the JWKS are KeycloakTokenDTO, KeycloakUserInfoDTO, KeycloakTokenClaimsDTO, KeycloakWellKnownDTO and KeycloakCertsDTO.
  • Typed Protocol Mapper Configs - Added one config DTO for each of 51 protocol mapper types (OIDC, SAML, oid4vc, docker-v2) in protocol_mapper_config_dtos, with to_config(), to_mapper(name), from_config() and parse_protocol_mapper_config().
  • Token Exchange Types - Added TokenExchangeTokenType and the token exchange and AuthZEN DTOs.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text:
• Calls python-keycloak Lacks - Added about 280 admin calls, made through the admin connection with its error handling.
    • Realms: list, delete, events, admin events, event settings, client policies, profiles, types, default groups, localization, partial import and export, logout-all, revocation push, session deletion, SMTP test
    • Users: filtered list and count, user profile, credentials, consents, federated identities, sessions, groups, impersonation, email actions
    • Clients: list, get, update, delete by UUID, secrets, registration token, scope evaluation, installation providers, nodes, session counts
    • Roles by name and by id, role mappings and scope mappings for users, groups, clients and client scopes
    • Identity providers with mappers, organizations (identity providers, members, invitations, groups and role mappings), required actions, authentication providers, realm keys, brute force detection, client initial access tokens, client certificates
    • Authorization services: settings, filtered lists, searches, resource and scope details, providers, policy and permission evaluation
    • Protocol mappers: get by id, bulk add, list by protocol
  • Token Exchange - token_exchange(KeycloakTokenExchangeRequestDTO) covers standard token exchange (V2), the delegation preview and the legacy fields, and can exchange a token for a JWT assertion.
  • JWT Authorization Grant - jwt_bearer_grant(assertion, scope) implements RFC 7523 and the identity assertion grant (ID-JAG). With token_exchange it chains identity across two realms.
  • RPT Requests - request_rpt(token, audience, permissions) performs the UMA ticket grant of the authz-client library.
  • AuthZEN - get_authzen_configuration, authzen_evaluation and authzen_evaluations call the experimental AuthZEN endpoints with the caller's own bearer token. Keycloak 26.8 rejects an evaluation without resource.type, so the DTO requires it.
  • Typed Mapper Calls - add_*_mapper_with_config, update_*_mapper_config and get_*_mapper_config add, replace and read a client scope or client protocol mapper from a typed config.
  • Request DTOs for Config - create_realm, update_realm, create_client, create_organization and update_organization accept an optional config request DTO next to their keyword arguments.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text:
• Resource Layout - breaking: the adapter is organized by Keycloak admin REST resource. The adapter_mixins and port_mixins packages are removed and resources/ and protocols/ are private (_resources, _protocols, _base, _connection, _type_aliases).
    • Import KeycloakAdapter, AsyncKeycloakAdapter, KeycloakPort, AsyncKeycloakPort and the Keycloak*Type names from archipy.adapters.keycloak.adapters and archipy.adapters.keycloak.ports
    • archipy.adapters.keycloak.auth is unchanged
  • DTO Return Types - behavior: methods that returned dict, bytes or a TypedDict return DTOs. isinstance(result, dict) is now false. The Keycloak*Type names for groups, roles, organizations, client scopes, protocol mappers and components are aliases of the DTOs.
  • Auth Context - behavior: AuthenticatedUserDTO.raw_user_info and token_info are KeycloakUserInfoDTO and KeycloakTokenClaimsDTO. The fastapi_auth dependency yields the user info DTO. request.state values are still deprecated dicts.
  • Not Found Mapping - behavior: every Keycloak 404 maps to ResourceNotFoundError, where some used to surface as InternalError.

docs.title: Not Supported
docs.text:

  • Non-JSON Bodies - Calls that send text/plain, multipart or form-encoded bodies are left out: user credential label, realm localization single text, client description converter, certificate uploads, organization invite-user and invite-existing-user.

docs.text:

  • UMA Permission Checks - permissions_check checks several permissions correctly.
    • python-keycloak joins them into one comma-separated form field, which Keycloak does not understand (python-keycloak issue 705)
    • The adapter sends one permission field each and returns True only when every requested permission is granted
  • Denied UMA Decisions - A UMA request that grants nothing raises InsufficientPermissionsError, where it used to surface as InternalError.

docs.title: Helpers - Pydantic AI Instrumentation
docs.text:
• Pydantic AI Auto-Instrumentation - Pydantic AI agents now export their traces and metrics through ArchiPy's OpenTelemetry providers.
    • OtelUtils initialization calls Agent.instrument_all with ArchiPy's tracer and meter providers when pydantic-ai-slim is installed
    • Agent runs (invoke_agent <name>), model requests (chat <model>) and tool calls (execute_tool <name>) become spans, and token usage becomes the gen_ai.client.token.usage metric
    • Delegated agents are traced under the calling tool, and agents run inside FastAPI or gRPC requests join the request trace
    • Settings an application installed itself with Agent.instrument_all are left alone
    • In Elastic APM an agent run inside a request is a span of the request transaction; an agent run outside a request is a root span, which APM types as unknown

docs.title: Configs - Pydantic AI
docs.text:
• PydanticAIConfig - Added the BaseConfig.PYDANTIC_AI section that controls the instrumentation.
    • INSTRUMENTATION_ENABLED (default true) turns the instrumentation off
    • INSTRUMENTATION_INCLUDE_CONTENT (default true) keeps prompts, model output and tool arguments and results in span attributes; turn it off when they hold personal or secret data
    • INSTRUMENTATION_INCLUDE_BINARY_CONTENT (default false) keeps images, audio and documents in span attributes
    • INSTRUMENTATION_INCLUDE_MODEL_REQUEST_PARAMETERS (default true), INSTRUMENTATION_VERSION (default 6, or 5) and INSTRUMENTATION_USE_AGGREGATED_USAGE_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES (default true) map to the matching InstrumentationSettings options

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text:
• Client Options - The Temporal client takes more of its settings from TEMPORAL config.
    • CONNECT_TIMEOUT bounds the TCP connection attempt, GRPC_COMPRESSION (gzip or none) controls gRPC compression (the SDK gzips by default since 1.29, which breaks proxies without gRPC compression), and PAYLOADS_WARN_SIZE / MEMO_WARN_SIZE set the payload and memo size warning limits
    • TLS_SERVER_NAME, TLS_VERIFICATION_SERVER_NAME and TLS_ENABLED add a server name override, a certificate-only name check that leaves SNI alone, and a TLS switch; the CA certificate alone now gives server-only TLS, and only a client certificate without its key (or the reverse) is rejected
    • METRICS_GLOBAL_TAGS adds tags to every SDK metric and SDK_CORE_LOG_LEVEL sets the log level of the SDK core
    • RUNTIME_DISABLE_ENVIRONMENT_INFO keeps runtime and hosting information out of worker heartbeats
    • TemporalAdapter and TemporalWorkerManager accept a data_converter and interceptors; client interceptors that also implement the worker interface apply to every worker the manager starts
  • Pydantic Payloads - Workflow and activity payloads use temporalio's Pydantic data converter by default (PYDANTIC_DATA_CONVERTER), so Pydantic models, datetimes and decimals round trip. Pass data_converter to add a payload codec for encryption or compression.
  • Worker Options - start_worker accepts tuner, activity_executor, deployment_config, workflow_failure_exception_types and workflow_runner; WORKER_POLLER_AUTOSCALING turns on poller autoscaling and WORKER_MAX_ACTIVITIES_PER_SECOND, WORKER_MAX_TASK_QUEUE_ACTIVITIES_PER_SECOND and WORKER_MAX_EAGER_ACTIVITY_RESERVATIONS set the rate limits and the eager reservations.
  • Workflow IDs - start_workflow and execute_workflow accept id_reuse_policy and id_conflict_policy, so a start can be idempotent with USE_EXISTING. Generated workflow and worker IDs are UUIDv7.
  • Workflow Listing - list_workflows takes a limit and the new iter_workflows pages through results without loading them all.
  • Schedules - Added pause_schedule, unpause_schedule, trigger_schedule, describe_schedule, update_schedule, list_schedules and delete_schedule; create_schedule accepts args and memo.
  • Domain Errors - Adapter calls raise ArchiPy errors instead of Temporal's: AlreadyExistsError (with the run_id and first_run_id of the running workflow), NotFoundError, UnavailableError, DeadlineExceededError, WorkerConnectionError and TemporalError.

docs.title: Adapters - MinIO
docs.text: • S3 Checksums and CA Bundle - REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION and RESPONSE_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION control the S3 checksums boto3 enables by default since 1.36 (older MinIO servers reject them), and CA_BUNDLE points to a CA bundle for certificate checks.

docs.title: Adapters - PostgreSQL
docs.text: • Connect Timeout - POSTGRES_SQLALCHEMY.CONNECT_TIMEOUT bounds the connection attempt; without it libpq waits indefinitely.

docs.title: Adapters - Elasticsearch
docs.text: • Retry Backoff - RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE and RETRY_BACKOFF_CAP add exponential backoff between retries; unset, the client keeps its own defaults.

docs.title: Adapters - Parsian IPG
docs.text: • SOAP Timeout - PARSIAN_SHAPARAK.TIMEOUT (default 30 seconds) bounds every SOAP operation.

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• Replay-Safe Logs - Log events recorded from workflow code use ReplaySafeLoggerProvider, so replays no longer duplicate them.
  • Metric Cardinality Limit - OTEL.METRICS_CARDINALITY_LIMIT caps the attribute sets per instrument; the rest fold into the otel.metric.overflow series.

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text:
• Activity Heartbeat Default - Behavior: ACTIVITY_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT defaults to None. The old 10 seconds failed every activity that does not heartbeat.
  • Workflow Timeouts - Behavior: WORKFLOW_RUN_TIMEOUT and WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT default to unbounded instead of 60 and 300 seconds. A run timeout above the execution timeout is still rejected, but the task timeout no longer has to be below the run timeout. A timeout of 0 passed to a call means unbounded.
  • Workflow Retries - Behavior: the RETRY_* policy is no longer applied to whole workflows, because a workflow retry reruns it from the start. Set WORKFLOW_RETRY_ENABLED to bring it back.
  • Activity Errors - Behavior: BaseActivity no longer logs the error message, only its type, and an ArchiPy error with a 4xx HTTP status fails the activity without retries. Override _is_non_retryable to change the rule.
  • Worker Shutdown - stop lets the SDK enforce the graceful shutdown timeout, and shutdown_all_workers stops workers concurrently.
  • Sandboxed Config - BaseWorkflow reads the host process configuration inside the workflow sandbox, and its activity and child workflow helpers default to the workflow's own task queue instead of a configured one.
  • SDK Pin - temporalio is capped below 2.

docs.title: Adapters - Kafka
docs.text:
• Hostname Verification - Behavior: SSL connections verify the broker hostname. SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM defaults to https; set it to none for brokers whose certificates do not match their address, which logs a warning.
  • Producer Close - close closes the producer instead of only flushing it, which also aborts an open transaction.

docs.title: Adapters - Vault
docs.text:
• Session Settings - The TLS and timeout settings (CA_CERT_PATH, VERIFY_SSL, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, READ_TIMEOUT) are applied. hvac copied the session's own verify over them and used a fixed 30 second timeout.
  • Parameterised Requests - get_dynamic_credentials with parameters calls write_data, avoiding hvac's deprecated write(data=...).

docs.title: Adapters - ScyllaDB
docs.text:
• Execution Profile - Policies and the request timeout are set in the default execution profile instead of the deprecated legacy Cluster arguments.
  • Pool Settings - Behavior: MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_HOST, MIN_CONNECTIONS_PER_HOST, CORE_CONNECTIONS_PER_HOST and MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION were never applied, because scylla-driver has no per-host pool sizing. They stay, and a DeprecationWarning names those set to a non-default value.

docs.title: Adapters - Keycloak
docs.text: • Async Token Validation - validate_token and get_token_info of the async adapter verify against every key of the realm's JWKS instead of one realm key, so they keep working after a key rotation, like the sync adapter.

docs.title: Adapters - Parsian IPG
docs.text: • Proxy for WSDL - The proxy is also used to load the WSDL in async mode, where zeep's own client bypassed it.

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• Pushgateway Grouping Key - Behavior: the Pushgateway grouping key gets an instance label unless one is configured: POD_NAME, else HOSTNAME or the host name. Several replicas used to share one group and overwrite each other's metrics, and a shutdown deleted the shared group. A pod that crashes leaves its group behind; see the observability tutorial.
  • Logging Handler - Log records ship through the LoggingHandler of opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging, which the otel extra now installs. The SDK's own handler is deprecated since OpenTelemetry 1.40 and remains the fallback.

docs.title: Adapters - Redis
docs.text: • Mock Protocol - The Redis mocks follow PROTOCOL, so their replies have the RESP3 shapes of a real client.

docs.title: Models - Keycloak
docs.text: • Validation Settings - The Keycloak DTOs use validate_by_name and validate_by_alias instead of populate_by_name.

docs.title: Adapters - Elasticsearch
docs.text: • Request Body - Search and index creation expand the request body into keyword arguments, avoiding the client's deprecation warning when both are passed.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• MySQL and StarRocks Error Codes - Database errors are classified by the MySQL error number before the SQLSTATE. pymysql 1.2 and asyncmy 0.2.14 attach a SQLSTATE to server errors, which made deadlocks serialization failures, lock timeouts connection errors and duplicate keys generic integrity errors.
  • StarRocks Connect Timeout - CONNECT_TIMEOUT is applied.
  • In-Memory SQLite - Connections of an in-memory database are no longer recycled, which discarded the database.
  • Async Extras - archipy-mysql[async], archipy-starrocks[async] and archipy-sqlite depend on sqlalchemy[asyncio], because SQLAlchemy 2.1 no longer installs greenlet.

docs.title: Adapters - Temporal
docs.text:
• Activity Cache Key - BaseActivity builds its cache key from a SHA-256 digest of the input. hash() is salted per process, so workers never shared a key.
  • Worker Failures - WorkerHandle tracks the worker run task: is_running turns False when it ends, and run_error holds the error that ended it.
  • Concurrent Clients - Concurrent first calls share one client.
  • Cancel Reason - cancel_workflow passes its reason.
  • Schedules - stop_schedule is deprecated for delete_schedule, because it deleted the schedule.
  • Atomic Activities - AtomicActivity.with_db_type returns a validated copy instead of raising NotImplementedError.
  • Runtime Errors - A Runtime that cannot be built raises ConfigurationError instead of silently dropping the SDK metrics.

docs.text: • New Scenarios - Replaying recorded histories to catch non-determinism, long timers in a time-skipping environment (start_time_skipping_v2), the heartbeat default, client and worker interceptors, the Pydantic round trip, error mapping, schedule management and the new client and worker options.

docs.title: Helpers - OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
• Per-Signal OTLP Headers - TRACES_HEADERS, METRICS_HEADERS and LOGS_HEADERS set the OTLP headers of one signal, so traces and logs can send a Bearer token while metrics send Basic credentials with X-Scope-OrgID and Tenant-ID.
    • A per-signal value replaces OTLP_HEADERS for that signal and is not merged with it
    • USE_STANDARD_ENV reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_HEADERS and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS; the OpenTelemetry parser lowercases header names
    • The Temporal SDK metrics runtime uses METRICS_HEADERS
  • OTLP TLS and mTLS - CERTIFICATE, CLIENT_CERTIFICATE, CLIENT_KEY and INSECURE configure TLS for the OTLP exporters, shared as OTLP_* and per signal as TRACES_*, METRICS_* and LOGS_*.
    • gRPC exporters get channel credentials built from the PEM files; HTTP exporters get the file paths and follow the URL scheme
    • A client certificate without a client key, or the reverse, is rejected
    • USE_STANDARD_ENV reads the matching OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables
  • Span and Attribute Limits - ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT, ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT, SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT, SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT, SPAN_EVENT_COUNT_LIMIT and SPAN_LINK_COUNT_LIMIT cap what a span keeps, and reach the tracer provider, including the replay-safe Temporal one, as SpanLimits. Unset keeps the SDK defaults; USE_STANDARD_ENV reads the matching OTEL_*_LIMIT variables.

docs.title: Tests - OpenTelemetry
docs.text: • New Scenarios - Per-signal headers on each exporter, the standard variable mapping for headers, TLS options and limits, TLS precedence and credentials, the client certificate and key pairing, and spans capped by the limits.

docs.title: Configs - BaseConfig
docs.text:
• APP_NAME identity field - Top-level APP_NAME is now a built-in BaseConfig setting (env: APP_NAME). On set_global(), customize() fills nested identity defaults when they are still unset or placeholders:
    • OTEL.SERVICE_NAME when None
    • FASTAPI.PROJECT_NAME when "project_name"
    • AUTH.JWT_ISSUER when "your-app-name"
    • TEMPORAL.CLIENT_IDENTITY when None
    • Explicit nested env values (OTEL__SERVICE_NAME, etc.) always win

docs.title: Adapters - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Sync path no longer requires greenlet - archipy[postgres,sqlalchemy] (and the MySQL, SQLite, and StarRocks equivalents) failed on import with SQLAlchemy 2.1, which no longer installs greenlet by default.
    • The base session manager imported sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio at module level; async names are now TYPE_CHECKING-only and imported lazily inside the async engine and session factory methods
    • Async adapters still need the sqlalchemy-async extra and raise SQLAlchemy's install hint without it
  • Pool arguments hook - Added _get_pool_kwargs() to both base session managers so dialects can adjust pool arguments for the pool class SQLAlchemy selects.

docs.title: Adapters - SQLite
docs.text:
• Driver matches adapter mode - Sync and async SQLite adapters share SQLiteSQLAlchemyConfig, whose default DRIVER_NAME is sqlite+aiosqlite, so the sync adapter needed aiosqlite installed.
    • The sync session manager swaps sqlite+aiosqlite for sqlite
    • The async session manager swaps sqlite / sqlite+pysqlite for sqlite+aiosqlite
    • Other explicitly configured drivers are used unchanged
  • In-memory databases - :memory:, empty, and mode=memory URI databases no longer fail with Invalid argument(s) 'pool_timeout','pool_use_lifo','max_overflow'.
    • Queue-pool-only arguments are dropped because SQLAlchemy uses SingletonThreadPool / StaticPool there

docs.title: Tests - SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
• Greenlet-free import scenarios - Added BDD scenarios asserting that importing each sync session manager module (Postgres, SQLite, MySQL, StarRocks) does not load sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.
  • SQLite driver and in-memory scenarios - Added BDD scenarios running sync and async SQLite adapters with either driver on in-memory and file databases.

docs.title: Tests - Configuration
docs.text:
• MinIO test image - Switched the MinIO testcontainer image to pgsty/minio; MinIO no longer publishes public images on Docker Hub and quay.io requires authentication.
  • Feature step lint - Resolved Ruff F errors in feature steps (duplicate step function names, unused imports and locals).

docs.title: Helpers - gRPC Interceptors
docs.text:
• Streaming RPCs with OpenTelemetry - Response-streaming RPCs failed under the async server with 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got coroutine.
    • BaseAsyncGrpcServerInterceptor wrapped every RPC type in a coroutine; unary_stream and stream_stream handlers are now wrapped in an async generator
    • Added an overridable intercept_stream hook; the default runs intercept around handler invocation and relays the stream, so existing subclasses keep working
    • Added iterate_stream_result, which handles async-generator handlers and coroutine-style handlers that push responses through context.write
  • Mid-stream error mapping - AsyncGrpcServerExceptionInterceptor and GrpcServerExceptionInterceptor now map errors raised while a stream is being consumed to gRPC statuses instead of UNKNOWN.
    • The sync interceptor guards any returned iterator, not only generators
  • Stream duration metrics - rpc.server.duration is now recorded when a stream finishes, with the status of any mid-stream error.
    • The sync metrics interceptor previously recorded duration as soon as the stream was created
    • Added AsyncGrpcServerOtelMetricsInterceptor.intercept_stream

docs.title: Tests - gRPC
docs.text:
• Streaming interceptor scenarios - Added BDD scenarios in otel.feature running a real local gRPC server, sync and async, with the exception, metrics, and full (contrib OTel, metrics, exception) interceptor stacks.
    • Unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional RPCs
    • Mid-stream error mapping, coroutine-style stream handlers, and sync plain-iterator handlers
    • Stream duration datapoints and status

docs.title: Tests - FastAPI
docs.text:
• Server-sent events scenarios - Added BDD scenarios in app_utils.feature and otel.feature that serve real ArchiPy FastAPI apps with uvicorn and stream text/event-stream responses.
    • Event delivery, incremental flushing (also with GZip enabled), and events kept after a mid-stream failure
    • Client disconnect, concurrent clients, CORS, TrustedHost, and pre-stream error mapping
    • OpenTelemetry server spans and HTTP server duration metrics for streamed responses

docs.title: Helpers - Keycloak
docs.text:
• Impersonation tracking - Request authentication now parses the RFC 8693 act claim emitted by Keycloak 26.8.
    • Nested act claims are flattened into an actor chain, outermost (current) actor first, capped at 8 entries
    • gRPC auth decorators set the actor chain on the auth context; FastAPI dependencies set request.state.actor_chain
    • Impersonated requests are logged at INFO with the subject and the full actor chain
    • propagation_headers() forwards the same bearer token so downstream services see the same act claim

• Per-extra adapter packages - Each adapter now ships as its own distribution, so archipy[redis] installs only the Redis adapter files instead of every adapter. Imports are unchanged (archipy.adapters.redis, ...).
    • New packages: archipy-redis, archipy-kafka, archipy-elasticsearch, archipy-minio, archipy-keycloak, archipy-scylladb, archipy-temporal, archipy-vault, archipy-postgres, archipy-mysql, archipy-sqlite, archipy-starrocks, archipy-parsian-ipg, archipy-saman-ipg

docs.text:
# configs/app_config.py
from archipy.configs.base_config import BaseConfig
from archipy.configs.environment_type import EnvironmentType


class AppConfig(BaseConfig):
    """Application-specific configuration.

    All ArchiPy sections (REDIS, POSTGRES, FASTAPI, …) are inherited from BaseConfig.
    APP_NAME is synced into nested identity fields by BaseConfig.customize().
    Override `customize` for other app-specific defaults after loading.
    """

    APP_NAME: str = "my-service"

    def customize(self) -> None:
        """Apply app-specific configuration overrides."""
        super().customize()
        self.FASTAPI.SERVE_HOST = "0.0.0.0"  # noqa: S104
        self.FASTAPI.SERVE_PORT = 8000
        self.FASTAPI.RELOAD = self.ENVIRONMENT == EnvironmentType.LOCAL


config = AppConfig()
BaseConfig.set_global(config)

# models/entities/user.py
import uuid

from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Synonym, mapped_column

from archipy.models.entities.sqlalchemy.base_entities import BaseEntity


class User(BaseEntity):
    """User domain entity."""

    __tablename__ = "users"

    user_uuid = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    pk_uuid = Synonym("user_uuid")

    username = mapped_column(String(100), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = mapped_column(String(255), unique=True, nullable=False)

docs.title: Domain Adapters
docs.text:
Domain adapters wrap an ArchiPy base adapter and own all entity construction and query logic for a single aggregate.

# repositories/user/adapters/user_db_adapter.py
import logging
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from archipy.adapters.postgres.sqlalchemy.adapters import PostgresSQLAlchemyAdapter

from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import CreateUserCommandDTO, SearchUsersQueryDTO, UserResponseDTO
from models.entities.user import User

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class UserDBAdapter:
    """Wraps PostgresSQLAlchemyAdapter for the User aggregate."""

    def __init__(self, db: PostgresSQLAlchemyAdapter) -> None:
        self._adapter = db

    def create_user(self, command: CreateUserCommandDTO) -> UserResponseDTO:
        """Persist a new User entity and return a response DTO.

        Args:
            command: Create command with username and email.

        Returns:
            Response DTO for the newly created user.
        """
        user = User(user_uuid=uuid4(), username=command.username, email=command.email)
        created = self._adapter.create(user)
        logger.debug("Created user %s", created.user_uuid)
        return UserResponseDTO(id=str(created.user_uuid), username=created.username, email=created.email)

    def get_user_by_id(self, query: "GetUserByIdQueryDTO") -> UserResponseDTO | None:
        """Retrieve a User by UUID.

        Args:
            query: Query with the target user UUID.

        Returns:
            Response DTO, or None if not found.
        """
        from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import GetUserByIdQueryDTO  # noqa: PLC0415

        user = self._adapter.get_by_uuid(User, query.user_id)
        if not user:
            return None
        return UserResponseDTO(id=str(user.user_uuid), username=user.username, email=user.email)

    def search_users(self, query: SearchUsersQueryDTO) -> list[UserResponseDTO]:
        """Search users by optional username filter.

        Args:
            query: Search filters.

        Returns:
            List of matching response DTOs.
        """
        users = self._adapter.filter_by(User, username=query.username, limit=query.limit)
        return [UserResponseDTO(id=str(u.user_uuid), username=u.username, email=u.email) for u in users]

# repositories/user/adapters/user_cache_adapter.py
import logging

from archipy.adapters.redis.ports import RedisPort

from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import UserResponseDTO

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_USER_TTL = 3600  # seconds


class UserCacheAdapter:
    """Cache adapter for the User aggregate — wraps a RedisPort implementation."""

    def __init__(self, cache: RedisPort) -> None:
        self._cache = cache

    def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> UserResponseDTO | None:
        """Read a cached user response DTO.

        Args:
            user_id: String UUID of the user.

        Returns:
            Cached UserResponseDTO, or None on cache miss.
        """
        import json  # noqa: PLC0415

        raw = self._cache.get(f"user:{user_id}")
        if raw is None:
            return None
        logger.debug("Cache hit for user %s", user_id)
        return UserResponseDTO.model_validate(json.loads(raw))

    def set_user(self, user_id: str, response: UserResponseDTO) -> None:
        """Write a user response DTO to the cache.

        Args:
            user_id: String UUID used as cache key suffix.
            response: DTO to serialise and store.
        """
        self._cache.set(f"user:{user_id}", response.model_dump_json(), ex=_USER_TTL)
        logger.debug("Cached user %s for %ds", user_id, _USER_TTL)

docs.text:
# repositories/user/user_repository.py
import logging

from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import (
    CreateUserCommandDTO,
    GetUserByIdQueryDTO,
    SearchUsersQueryDTO,
    UserResponseDTO,
)
from repositories.user.adapters.user_cache_adapter import UserCacheAdapter
from repositories.user.adapters.user_db_adapter import UserDBAdapter

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class UserRepository:
    """Orchestrates DB and cache adapters for the User aggregate."""

    def __init__(self, db_adapter: UserDBAdapter, cache_adapter: UserCacheAdapter) -> None:
        self._db = db_adapter
        self._cache = cache_adapter

    def create_user(self, command: CreateUserCommandDTO) -> UserResponseDTO:
        """Create a new user and prime the cache.

        Args:
            command: Create command with username and email.

        Returns:
            Response DTO for the new user.
        """
        response = self._db.create_user(command)
        self._cache.set_user(response.id, response)
        return response

    def get_user_by_id(self, query: GetUserByIdQueryDTO) -> UserResponseDTO | None:
        """Return a user by ID, reading from cache first.

        Args:
            query: Query with the target user UUID.

        Returns:
            Response DTO, or None if the user does not exist.
        """
        cached = self._cache.get_user(str(query.user_id))
        if cached:
            return cached
        response = self._db.get_user_by_id(query)
        if response:
            self._cache.set_user(response.id, response)
        return response

    def search_users(self, query: SearchUsersQueryDTO) -> list[UserResponseDTO]:
        """Search users by optional username filter (always hits the DB).

        Args:
            query: Search filters.

        Returns:
            List of matching response DTOs.
        """
        return self._db.search_users(query)

docs.text:
# logics/user/user_registration_logic.py
import logging

from archipy.adapters.base.sqlalchemy.atomic import postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic

from models.dtos.user.domain.v1.user_dtos import UserRegistrationInputDTO, UserRegistrationOutputDTO
from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import CreateUserCommandDTO, SearchUsersQueryDTO
from models.errors.user_errors import UserAlreadyExistsError
from repositories.user.user_repository import UserRepository

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class UserRegistrationLogic:
    """Business logic for registering new users."""

    def __init__(self, user_repository: UserRepository) -> None:
        self._repo = user_repository

    @postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic
    def register_user(self, input_dto: UserRegistrationInputDTO) -> UserRegistrationOutputDTO:
        """Validate uniqueness and persist a new user.

        Args:
            input_dto: Registration data from the service layer.

        Returns:
            Output DTO for the newly created user.

        Raises:
            UserAlreadyExistsError: If the username is already taken.
        """
        existing = self._repo.search_users(SearchUsersQueryDTO(username=input_dto.username, limit=1))
        if existing:
            raise UserAlreadyExistsError(
                resource_type="user",
                additional_data={"username": input_dto.username},
            )
        created = self._repo.create_user(
            CreateUserCommandDTO(username=input_dto.username, email=input_dto.email),
        )
        return UserRegistrationOutputDTO(id=created.id, username=created.username, email=created.email)

# logics/user/user_query_logic.py
import logging

from archipy.adapters.base.sqlalchemy.atomic import postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic
from archipy.models.errors import NotFoundError

from models.dtos.user.domain.v1.user_dtos import (
    UserGetInputDTO,
    UserGetOutputDTO,
    UserSearchInputDTO,
    UserSearchOutputDTO,
    UserSummaryOutputDTO,
)
from models.dtos.user.repository.user_dtos import GetUserByIdQueryDTO, SearchUsersQueryDTO
from repositories.user.user_repository import UserRepository

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class UserQueryLogic:
    """Business logic for querying user data."""

    def __init__(self, user_repository: UserRepository) -> None:
        self._repo = user_repository

    @postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic
    def get_user_by_id(self, input_dto: UserGetInputDTO) -> UserGetOutputDTO:
        """Retrieve a user by ID.

        Args:
            input_dto: Contains the UUID of the user.

        Returns:
            Output DTO for the matched user.

        Raises:
            NotFoundError: If no user with the given ID exists.
        """
        user = self._repo.get_user_by_id(GetUserByIdQueryDTO(user_id=input_dto.user_id))
        if not user:
            raise NotFoundError(resource_type="user", additional_data={"user_id": str(input_dto.user_id)})
        return UserGetOutputDTO(id=user.id, username=user.username, email=user.email)

    @postgres_sqlalchemy_atomic
    def search_users(self, input_dto: UserSearchInputDTO) -> UserSearchOutputDTO:
        """Search users by optional username filter.

        Args:
            input_dto: Search filters from the service layer.

        Returns:
            Output DTO wrapping the list of matched users.
        """
        results = self._repo.search_users(SearchUsersQueryDTO(username=input_dto.username, limit=input_dto.limit))
        return UserSearchOutputDTO(
            users=[UserSummaryOutputDTO(id=u.id, username=u.username, email=u.email) for u in results],
        )
